answer: Client-puzzle with server-chosen difficulty resists sybils: the node issues each registrant a fresh puzzle whose difficulty the server raises adaptively when registration volume spikes, so a flood automatically faces harder puzzles. A relic of steady honest joins sees easy puzzles; a cipher-burst of mass registration drives difficulty up for everyone in that wave, taxing the attacker most. The nadir of cost is for low-volume honest joiners; a farm attempting bulk creation triggers the adaptive difficulty climb and pays escalating compute per identity exactly when it tries to scale.
